title.narrative: Emergency provision of integrated health, nutrition, FSL and WASH assistance to vulnerable conflict affected populations in Habila, Heiban and Dilling localities of South Kordofan state

description.narrative: ltpgtSouth Kordofan State currently hosts 4% of the IDP caseload in Sudan (IOM DTM, update Oct 2024). Humanitarian needs in South Kordofan remain critically high due to ongoing conflict and limited access to humanitarian aid, with particularly severe challenges in the localities of Habila, Heiban and Dilling. The influx of IDPs is straining food security and nutrition, especially for vulnerable groups, such as children. The majority of IDP and host community households and they face barriers to accessing healthcare, WASH and other basic services due to the disruption of supplies, infrastructure damages, displacements, and imposed restrictions.ltbrgtSave the Children (SC), in partnership National NGO Omarang Charity Acts and Mentorship (OCAM), proposes this multi-sector project to support 55,230 people, including the most vulnerable children and families, to meet basic needs and reduce high morbidity, acute malnutrition, disease outbreaks and exposure by increasing access to integrated, disability-inclusive and gender-sensitive health, nutrition, Shelter/NFI, FSL and WASH services in Habila, Heiban and Dilling Localities. ltbrgtTo achieve this, the project will contribute to improving equitable and inclusive access to quality life-saving curative and preventative healthcare services through three health facilities, covering prioritized locations with the most vulnerable populations. ltbrgtTo fill identified health and nutrition gaps including medical supplies, incentives, minor rehabilitation and referrals and increase the coverage, the project will target women of reproductive age, with a focus on pregnant and lactating women, and children under 5 years of age, while providing gender-sensitive and disability-inclusive lifesaving healthcare for communicable and non-communicable diseases among children over 5, adults and the elderly. ltbrgtThe project will deliver safe, timely, principled, and gender-responsive WASH assistance to 5,600 people, prioritizing vulnerable groups such as women, men, children, and persons with disabilities. Key interventions include equipping four targeted health facilities with essential WASH infrastructure and materials, such as water purification systems, excreta disposal facilities, cleaning supplies, and solid waste management systems. Additionally, the project will ensure that targeted communities gain access to safe WASH services, including water trucking, the installation of four handpumps, and comprehensive hygiene promotion activities.ltbrgtThe project aims to significantly reduce mortality and morbidity rates among the critically food insecure vulnerable population in Heiban locality by supporting 18,000 people receive agriculture input, including seeds, tools while also enhancing their skills on good agricultural practices. The project aims to increasing target households’ ability to involve own food production to sustain themselves against food insecurity whilst restoring their livelihoods. SCI will conduct household-level targeting to identify the most vulnerable people through an integrated approach using different assessments using food security and socio-economic vulnerabilities The provision of the agriculture input will be used to restore livelihoods of the targeted most needy vulnerable people in accordance with the seasonal farming calendar in South Kordofanltbrgtlt/pgt
